subject: literature
passage: When his daughter asked whether he minded selling the old fishing boat, Henrik shrugged and said it was only wood and paint. He had not taken it out in years, he pointed out, and someone else might as well use it. Yet every evening that week he walked down to the harbor to check its ropes, and on the morning the buyer came, Ingrid found him polishing its brass fittings one last time. His claim of indifference, she decided, had been ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Henrik says the boat is "only wood and paint," but "Yet" introduces actions that show he cares deeply: checking its ropes every evening and polishing it one last time. His claim not to care was therefore not sincere. A show of feeling that hides one's real feeling is pretended, so "pretended" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests that Henrik's attitude spread to anyone else.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Henrik's daily visits and final polishing show that he cared about the boat, so his claim of not caring was not genuine.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Henrik gives a practical-sounding reason for selling, but Ingrid's conclusion is based on his behavior, which shows that his indifference was not real; whether his reasoning was sensible is not the point.
explanation.D: Correct. Henrik's actions contradict his words, so Ingrid concludes that his indifference was only pretended.
